prompt: Why is Vitest the test runner this lesson uses?

choices.text: It reads the same `vite.config.js` and plugins, so a `.vue` file runs as the dev server serves it
choices.why: Right. Vitest is Vite running tests, which is why there is almost nothing to configure.

choices.text: It runs every test in a real browser
choices.why: The tests run in jsdom, a document written in JavaScript, with no browser at all.

choices.text: It ships inside Vue, so it needs no install
choices.why: It was installed with `npm install --save-dev`, pinned to 5.0.5, beside two other packages.

choices.text: It is the one runner that reads TypeScript test files
choices.why: TypeScript is not the reason the lesson gives; the reason is that it shares Vite's configuration.

prompt: Before any test file existed, `npx vitest run` stopped. With what exit code?
hint: The line that says no test files were found.

prompt: The `test` script is `vitest`, with nothing after it. What does `npm test` do?

choices.text: Runs every test once and stops
choices.why: That is `vitest run`; without `run`, Vitest does not stop.

choices.text: Runs only the tests that failed on the last run
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson filters by the last result; it runs the files that match.

choices.text: Stays open and runs the tests again whenever a file changes
choices.why: Right. That is the watch mode, which is how it is used while working.

choices.text: Starts the dev server on port 5173 and tests the page it serves
choices.why: The tests mount components in jsdom; no server is started, which is why the dev server can be stopped.

prompt: The tidy `weekStart` counted back `date.getDay() - 1` days. What did the run report?
hint: What does `getDay()` return on a Sunday?

choices.text: Both `weekStart` tests failed, since the formula changed for every day
choices.why: For Monday to Saturday the two formulas agree, so the Wednesday test still passed.

choices.text: One failure, the Sunday test
choices.why: Right. `getDay()` is 0 on a Sunday, so it moved forwards to the next Monday: received 2026-10-26.

choices.text: No failure; the two formulas are the same thing written differently
choices.why: They agree six days in seven. On a Sunday the tidy one gives -1, and the test caught it.

choices.text: The `addDays` test, at the end of the month
choices.why: `addDays` was not touched by the edit, and its test passed.

prompt: `toBe` compares with `===`. To compare an object or a list field by field, a test uses `expect(value).___(…)`.
A new test of the planner writes `new Date(2026, 11, 25)`. Which day is that?
hint: How does JavaScript count the months?

choices.text: 25 November 2026
choices.why: That counts the months from one; JavaScript counts them from zero, so 11 is December.

choices.text: 26 December 2026
choices.why: Only the month counts from zero. The day of the month is the number written, 25.

choices.text: 11 December 2026, reading the arguments as year, day and month
choices.why: The order is year, month, day, as in `new Date(2026, 9, 21)` for 21 October.

choices.text: Christmas Day 2026
choices.why: Right. Month 11, counted from zero, is December, so this is 25 December 2026.

prompt: Why does each `SessionRow` test begin with `setActivePinia(createPinia())`?
hint: The row reads the course titles from somewhere.

choices.text: `mount` refuses a component that has no router
choices.why: The row needs a store, not a router; the router appears only in the week page's stubs.

choices.text: It gives each test a fresh, empty store, so no test sees another's data
choices.why: Right. Without it, the second test's title would still be in the third test's store.

choices.text: It makes the store fetch `courses.json` before the row is drawn
choices.why: A new Pinia starts empty and loads nothing; the second test puts the titles in by hand.

choices.text: Pinia keeps every store in `localStorage` between tests unless it is replaced
choices.why: Pinia keeps its stores in memory; `localStorage` is where the planner's own watcher saves the sessions.

prompt: Which of these do the `SessionRow` tests use to check the row? Choose all that apply.
hint: What a reader sees, and what the row tells its parent.

choices.text: `row.text()`
choices.why: Right. It is what a reader sees, compared with the whole sentence.

choices.text: `row.vm.title`, the computed inside the row
choices.why: The lesson warns against it: reaching into the component breaks on every refactoring.

choices.text: `row.classes()`
choices.why: Right. It returned `['done', 'today']`.

choices.text: `row.emitted('toggle')`
choices.why: Right. It listed one `toggle`, carrying `s4`.

prompt: Somebody rewrites `SessionRow` with different refs and computeds, and it draws exactly the same row. Which of its four tests break?

choices.text: The two title tests, because the computed that picks the title changed
choices.why: They read `text()`, the sentence drawn, and that did not change.

choices.text: None of them
choices.why: Right. They check what the row draws and emits, never how it decides, which is the point.

choices.text: The toggle test, since what a component emits is part of its insides
choices.why: What the row emits is what it tells its parent, its outside; the rewrite emits the same `toggle`.

choices.text: All four, as the file they mount is a different file now
choices.why: The tests import `SessionRow.vue` by name and read what it draws; the file's contents are not compared.

prompt: Why does the form test put `await` in front of `setValue` and `trigger`?

choices.text: Each one sends a request to the server and waits for the reply
choices.why: No request is involved; the form adds to a store in memory.

choices.text: Vue redraws on its next tick, and the promise settles once it has
choices.why: Right. Without the `await`, the next line would read the page from before the change.

choices.text: Called without it, they throw
choices.why: They return a promise either way; leaving out the `await` throws nothing, it reads too early.

choices.text: `v-model.number` converts `'25'` on a timer, and the `await` waits for it
choices.why: The conversion happens in the event handler; what is waited for is Vue's redraw.

prompt: After the empty form is sent, its test also checks `expect(usePlannerStore().sessions).toEqual([])`. What does that line hold the form to?
hint: Showing errors is half of it.

choices.text: That `beforeEach` emptied the store before the test began
choices.why: `beforeEach` sets up the store; this line is about what the form did after it was sent.

choices.text: That the courses failed to load
choices.why: The courses are put in by `beforeEach`, and `sessions` is a different list.

choices.text: That an invalid form added nothing
choices.why: Right. An invalid form must show its errors and must not have added a session.

choices.text: That the form cleared its own fields once the errors were shown
choices.why: The line reads the store, not the fields.

prompt: Vue Test Utils finds a field by its selector. The companion library built around finding it by its `<label>`, as a screen reader user does, is `@___-library/vue`.
A store test calls `planner.load()` three times at once. How many calls does the fake `fetch` record?
Right after `planner.toggle('s1')`, the copy in `localStorage` still has the session not done. Why?

choices.text: jsdom writes `localStorage` in the background
choices.why: jsdom's `localStorage` is written the moment `setItem` is called; the delay is in the store.

choices.text: `toggle` is an asynchronous action the test forgot to await
choices.why: The test awaits `nextTick()` on purpose, and it is the watcher that waits, not `toggle`.

choices.text: The store saves with a `watch`, which runs before the next render
choices.why: Right. After `await nextTick()` the saved copy is the new one.

choices.text: `beforeEach` cleared it, and nothing writes it again until the next `load`
choices.why: The copy was written at load, with the session not done; the toggle is what has not been saved yet.

prompt: What does the store test's `answer(body, status)` helper do? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Makes a `vi.fn` that records how it was called
choices.why: Right. That is what `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` reads.

choices.text: Starts a small server on a local port for the store to call
choices.why: No server is involved: the test must not depend on one being up.

choices.text: Puts it where the store looks for `fetch`, with `vi.stubGlobal`
choices.why: Right. The store calls `fetch` as usual and gets the fake.

choices.text: Answers with a real `Response`
choices.why: Right. So the store reads it with `response.ok` and `response.json()` as it reads a server's.

choices.text: Puts the real `fetch` back when the test ends
choices.why: That is `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach`, not the helper.

prompt: In the midnight test, what does `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(60_000)` do?

choices.text: Waits a real minute for `useToday`'s interval to fire
choices.why: The test takes about a tenth of a second; nothing waits for real.

choices.text: Sets the clock to sixty seconds past midnight
choices.why: `vi.setSystemTime` moved the clock, to 00:00:30, on the line before.

choices.text: Lets a minute pass at once, running the timers that fall due
choices.why: Right. `useToday`'s minute timer runs and moves today to the 22nd.

choices.text: Calls `useToday`'s callback directly, skipping the timer
choices.why: That would test a function and not the page, which is what fake timers avoid.

prompt: Why does the week page's test mount it with `stubs: { RouterLink: true, Teleport: true }`?
hint: Neither is what this test is about.

choices.text: jsdom cannot draw a link or a dialog
choices.why: jsdom draws both; a `RouterLink` needs a router, and a `Teleport` draws elsewhere.

choices.text: Stubbed components load faster, and the test has to finish within a second
choices.why: Speed is not the reason given; there is no such limit in the lesson.

choices.text: No router for the link, and the dialog would leave the wrapper
choices.why: Right. A `RouterLink` needs a router, and with the stub lesson 15's dialog is drawn where it is written, not in a `<body>` the wrapper does not read.

choices.text: So the test fails if either of them is drawn
choices.why: A stub draws an empty stand-in; it asserts nothing about whether it was drawn.

prompt: A colleague's test waits with `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))` before reading the page. What does the lesson say about it?

choices.text: It is fine as long as 500 ms is longer than the page ever takes
choices.why: How long the page takes depends on the machine, which is what makes the test fail now and then.

choices.text: It is the right wait once fake timers are on
choices.why: With fake timers a `setTimeout` does not run until the test lets time pass, so it would hang.

choices.text: It is `flushPromises()` written longhand
choices.why: `flushPromises()` waits for the promises already started, whatever their duration; this waits a fixed time and hopes.

choices.text: It fails on a busy machine one run in twenty, and a test that fails at times is worse than none
choices.why: Right. A wait should name what it waits for; if no tool can, the code should return its promise.

prompt: What does the lesson say a coverage report is?

choices.text: A target: the suite is finished at 100%
choices.why: A test written to raise the number checks that a line ran, not that it was right.

choices.text: The list of tests that passed and failed
choices.why: That is the run's own summary; coverage reports which lines ran.

choices.text: A map of what nobody tested
choices.why: Right. It is a map, not a target.

choices.text: Something Vitest prints on every run, with nothing to install
choices.why: It needs `--coverage` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` installed.

prompt: Which of these do the planner's tests leave out on purpose? Choose all that apply.
hint: The list of what these tests do not do.

choices.text: Checking that a `computed` recomputes
choices.why: Right. That is Vue's job to test, and it fails only when the framework does.

choices.text: The Sunday case of `weekStart`
choices.why: That is the test that caught the tidy refactoring.

choices.text: `CourseView` and the router
choices.why: Right. Each would need a router or a browser for little logic; the guard would be next.

choices.text: How the dialog traps focus
choices.why: Right. jsdom has no real focus or `<dialog>`; that belongs to a browser test.

choices.text: What `SessionRow` emits when its box is ticked
choices.why: The fourth `SessionRow` test checks exactly that, with `emitted('toggle')`.

prompt: The whole suite took about two seconds, while each file's tests took under 130 ms. Where did most of the time go?

choices.text: Type-checking the test files before running them
choices.why: `vue-tsc` is a separate command, `npm run type-check`, run after the suite.

choices.text: Making five jsdom documents, one per file
choices.why: Right. 77% of the tracked time, the price of no file seeing another's tests.

choices.text: The fake `fetch` waiting out a network timeout
choices.why: The fake answers at once with a `Response`; no network is touched.

choices.text: Vite starting the dev server so the page tests have something to load
choices.why: No server starts; the page is mounted in jsdom like the components.

prompt: Put the steps of the midnight test in the order they happen.
hint: `beforeEach` first, then `page()`, then the test's own lines.
items: Fake the clock at ten on 21 October
Load the store and mount the page
Check that today's row is 21 October
Set the system time to 00:00:30 on the 22nd
Check that today's row is 22 October

prompt: Match each thing a test needs to the tool the lesson uses for it.
hint: One tool on the right is the one the lesson rejects.

pairs.left: Wait for the promises already started, then the redraw
Make `new Date()` say what the test says
Replace `fetch` where the store looks for it
A fresh, empty store for each test

prompt: A new rule arrives: the minutes still to do this week, shown on the week page. Following the lesson's shape, where does most of its testing go?
hint: Where are the cheapest and most precise tests?

choices.text: Into the week page's test, with a fake clock and a fake `fetch`
choices.why: That works, but each case then costs a store, a clock and a mount; the page needs a line at most.

choices.text: Into a plain function in `planner.ts`, tested with a value in and an answer out
choices.why: Right. Rules in plain functions, components thin enough to need few tests.

choices.text: Into a Playwright test, as it appears on a page
choices.why: A browser test is for what jsdom lacks, such as focus; a sum of minutes needs no browser.

choices.text: Into nothing new: coverage of `HomeView` already runs those lines
choices.why: A line that ran is not a line that was right; coverage is a map, not a target.
